edbDesc: A kind of luminescence produced during electrochemical reactions in solutions. In electrogenerated chemiluminescence, electrochemically generated intermediates undergo a highly exergonic reaction to produce an electronically excited state that then emits light.
title: Electrochemiluminescence
description: Certain chemicals glow when a small voltage at an electrode sets off a light-giving reaction, so the light can be switched on exactly when and where you want it. Chemists worked it out in the 1960s. It is the heart of hospital blood analysers that count tiny amounts of hormones, cancer markers and heart-attack proteins.
effect: an electrode reaction makes a chemical glow
usedIn: Roche Elecsys immunoassay analysers (thyroid, cancer marker and troponin tests)
strength: The glow is too faint to see, but a light detector can count it down to a few billionths of a gram per litre.
pickWhy: Borderline: Rules don't settle whether it is its own card or a variant of chemiluminescence (another batch); I kept it because the use is distinct. No single discoverer (1960s, Hercules and Bard among others), so year and inventor are null.
